project.name: nl2odrl
project.description: NL-to-ODRL agentic converter: a fixed-stage pipeline that turns natural-language access rules into W3C ODRL 2.2 policies, with a typed IR, a deterministic compiler and SHACL validation.

nodes.summary: Package initializer for odrl_agent that declares the package and its public metadata.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Excludes virtualenvs, caches, node_modules, local databases, traces, reports and .env files from the Docker build context.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Two-stage Docker build: compiles the React studio with Node 22, then installs the odrl_agent Python package on python:3.12-slim, copies policies, prompts, schemas and scenarios, and serves on port 8901 with a healthcheck.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build keeps Node toolchain out of the final Python runtime image; the built UI is copied in with COPY --from=ui.

nodes.name: ui (build stage)
nodes.summary: Node 22 build stage that runs npm ci and npm run build for the ui-react frontend.

nodes.name: python (runtime stage)
nodes.summary: Python 3.12 runtime stage that installs the package, bundles the built UI, exposes 8901 and runs odrl-host serve.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Compose definition of the studio service built from the Dockerfile, with env-driven LLM, auth, queue and AgentCrash settings, persistent db and trace volumes, and an HTTP healthcheck.

nodes.name: studio
nodes.summary: Single compose service publishing port 8901 and passing environment variables for model endpoint, API keys, worker queue and cookie security.

nodes.name: bench-live.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that runs the live-model benchmark nightly, on manual dispatch, and on PRs touching extractor, LLM, IR, grounder, pipeline, prompts or pins. PRs block only on regressions against Baseline v1; nightly runs enforce all absolute targets and upload a JSON report.
nodes.languageNotes: Fails fast when LLAMA_API_KEY/LLAMA_BASE_URL secrets are missing; uses a concurrency group to cancel superseded runs.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: Main CI workflow with converter, studio and image jobs. It runs pytest on Python 3.11-3.13, a chaos gate, benchmark integrity and offline gates, and a PII guardrail via agentcrash. It then builds the React studio with Node 22 and the self-host Docker image.
nodes.languageNotes: Matrix build over Python versions; the image job depends on converter and studio via needs.

nodes.name: env-state.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema for the post-run environment snapshot (env_state/v1) holding run id, documents, record versions and a sha256 ledger hash.

nodes.name: policy-patch.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema for a diagnoser-proposed recovery-policy diff (policy_patch/v1) with source run id, rationale and a free-form patch object.

nodes.name: policy.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema for the recovery policy (policy/v1): rules keyed by trigger (timeout, mutating retry, untrusted content, stale read) with actions such as fail, retry_same or require_confirmation, and retry limits of at most 3 attempts.

nodes.name: scenario.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema for a scenario declaration (scenario/v1): task, seed, tool latency/timeout/mutating flags, invariants and the recovery policy name.

nodes.name: trace-event.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema for one JSONL trace event envelope (trace/v1) with hash-chained event ids, virtual timestamp, tool, outcome enum, latency, injector event and policy decision.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README describes the NL-to-ODRL pipeline architecture, benchmark and release gates. Start here to see how natural-language access rules become W3C ODRL 2.2 policies, and how the project checks and publishes them.

tour.title: CLI and Service Entry
tour.description: cli.py is the odrl-host entry point, with subcommands to run conversions, manage keys and serve the API. The serve command builds the FastAPI app in app.py, which wires auth, metrics and request logging around the run registry.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI uses an application factory function to assemble the app with its middleware and routes, which makes the service easy to configure and test.

tour.title: Typed PolicyIR
tour.description: ir.py defines the typed PolicyIR as Pydantic models for rules, constraints, duties, spans and ambiguities. Every later stage reads or writes this intermediate form, so the LLM output is validated before anything is compiled.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic models validate data at runtime from type annotations, so malformed LLM output fails early with clear errors.

tour.title: Extraction with an LLM
tour.description: Building on PolicyIR from Step 3, the extractor splits and classifies sentences, builds prompts and parses the model reply into PolicyIR. The llm.py client adds structured output, retry and backoff, and usage accounting, while netguard.py rejects unsafe LLM base URLs.

tour.title: Deterministic Compiler
tour.description: The compiler turns the typed PolicyIR into ODRL 2.2 JSON-LD with minted IRIs and canonical output. No LLM is involved here, so the same IR always yields the same policy. odrl.py supplies the ontology, JSON-LD contexts and RDF conversion.

tour.title: ODRL Vocabulary and SHACL
tour.description: The bundled ODRL 2.2 ontology, JSON-LD context and SHACL shapes are the standard the output is checked against. The shapes also pin vocabulary lists, which lets validation run locally without fetching anything.
tour.languageLesson: Turtle (.ttl) is a compact RDF syntax, and SHACL shapes written in it describe constraints that an RDF graph must satisfy.

tour.title: Grounding and Z3 Reasoning
tour.description: The grounder checks party and asset names against an entity catalog and flags unknown or suspicious ones. reasoning.py uses Z3 to encode constraints and the action hierarchy, so conflicts between compiled rules are found formally.

tour.title: Pipeline and Publish Gate
tour.description: pipeline.py orchestrates extraction, grounding, compilation, SHACL and Z3 checks end to end. The publish gate in publish.py stores drafts and lists blocking findings, so a human must approve before a policy is released.

tour.title: React Studio UI
tour.description: The React studio converts rules, browses policies and reviews drafts through a typed client for the FastAPI backend. Vite builds it into the ui folder, which the backend serves.
tour.languageLesson: React function components use hooks such as useState and useEffect, and a typed API client keeps the TypeScript interfaces in line with backend responses.

tour.title: Benchmark and Quality Gates
tour.description: The bench package generates tiered cases with gold PolicyIR, runs them through the pipeline and computes metrics. Gates compare the results to thresholds and a baseline, and pins detect drift in schema artifacts.

tour.title: Resilience and Chaos Testing
tour.description: Scenarios, schemas and policies drive AgentCrash-style testing of the conversion workflow. chaos.py re-runs the real pipeline under injected faults, and verifiers.py checks traces for ODRL validity, SHACL conformance and attacker influence.
tour.languageLesson: YAML scenario files declare tasks, tools and invariants as data, so the same harness can run a clean and a poisoned variant.

tour.title: Packaging, Docker and CI
tour.description: The Dockerfile builds the React studio with Node first, then installs the Python package in a second stage. docker-compose runs the studio service, and the CI workflow runs tests, studio and image jobs, with a nightly live benchmark workflow.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds separate build tools from the runtime image, which keeps the final image smaller.
